quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then proceed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. After stopping, you can go when it is safe and the way is clear.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane with the broken line.
You can pass from the lane with the solid line.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can only pass if you are in the lane with the broken line.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady green arrow traffic signal?

options.text: Move into the lane where the arrow points.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting other traffic and pedestrians pass.
Drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting other traffic and pedestrians pass.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane and let any vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection pass first.

questions.question: What should you do when you approach an accident scene?

options.text: Focus on your own driving.
Keep driving.
Stop only if you are involved or emergency help is not there yet.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or help has not arrived. Stay focused on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not stop just to look at an accident, fire, or other emergency.

questions.question: Why should you be careful when passing a bicycle?

options.text: Your car is faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.
The cyclist might swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist might swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.
questions.explanation: Always be careful passing bicycles. A cyclist may suddenly swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road. Always drive carefully near bicycles.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand point upward. What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand point upward, they are signaling a right turn. Adjust your driving if you are following this driver.

questions.question: What do regulatory signs do?

options.text: They are placed wherever there is immediate danger.
They tell drivers what they must or must not do.
They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
They warn that you are near a school zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tell drivers what they must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black text on white. They tell drivers what rules to follow. They can show speed limits, no passing zones, turn restrictions, and other driving rules.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see it.
Pull to the curb and check if it is on your street.
Slow down but do not stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and check if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but do not know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure it is not coming toward you.

questions.question: When should you leave extra space in front of your car when stopped?

options.text: On a hill going upward.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a hill going upward.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your car when stopped on an uphill slope. If the car in front rolls backward when traffic moves, extra space reduces the chance of a crash.

questions.question: Which tip does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Know that tinted windows make it harder to see at night.
Carry a flashlight in your car.
Look directly into the headlights of oncoming cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look directly into the headlights of oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: Do not look into oncoming headlights. This makes your pupils contract. After the car passes, your eyes need time to adjust back to normal light. During this time, you cannot see well.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
After you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Get into the exit lane well in advance. Do not slow down until after you have moved into the exit lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
No right turn.
All traffic must go straight.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road joins from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is ahead. A road joins from the right.

questions.question: A leaky exhaust system is dangerous because it can cause:

options.text: Loss of hearing.
Pollution.
Carbon monoxide poisoning.
Poor engine performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes exhaust gas from your vehicle and prevents fumes from entering the passenger area. Keep your exhaust system free of leaks. Fix all broken parts right away to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Two-way left turn.
Two-way traffic.
Minimum speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: One-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers which direction they must drive on a one-way street.

questions.question: What should a driver do at an uncontrolled intersection?

options.text: Keep driving at the same speed.
Stop, look both ways, and then proceed.
Yield to all other drivers.
Be ready to yield if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield if needed.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no stop sign or traffic light, yield to vehicles coming from the right. Always be ready to yield to avoid a crash. Do this by slowing down, covering the brake, and looking left, right, and left again.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow arrow?

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
Come to a complete stop.
You may turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
You have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic will stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in that direction. But oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must yield to them and to pedestrians.

questions.question: A fire engine is following your car on a two-lane street without using emergency lights. What should you do?

options.text: Drive normally.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down, move to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive normally.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is following you without lights or sirens, you do not need to move. Drive normally.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:

options.text: Safe to cross because trains rarely come.
Dangerous.
Safe places to park.
Places where you must always stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous.
questions.explanation: Always treat railroad crossings as dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and directions from flaggers. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what can you do?

options.text: You may turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You cannot turn and must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You no longer need to turn in the arrow's direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow changes to solid green, you may still turn in that direction. But first, yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: An approaching driver has not dimmed their high beams. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If an approaching driver does not dim their high beams, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you see the road until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop and look for other vehicles, then go if it is safe.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Slow down and go carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light tells you to slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: When can you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When you are turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are turning.
questions.explanation: You may cross a solid yellow line only when you are making a turn. In general, you cannot cross solid lines, but you can cross broken lines.

questions.question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and you can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and you cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: When should you come to a complete stop, yield to cross traffic and pedestrians, and then go through an intersection?

options.text: At a solid red light.
At a flashing yellow light.
At a solid green light.
At a flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the car to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the car to go.
questions.explanation: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the car to go. Once the car straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: How should you use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before you enter the exit ramp.
Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep the same speed on the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until you are on the exit ramp.

questions.question: Your car's gas pedal gets stuck while you are driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Slam on the brakes hard.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn off the engine carefully, without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine carefully, without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If the gas pedal sticks, turn off the engine using care to stop the engine only and not lock the steering wheel. Then apply the brakes and move to a safe area.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Side road.
Two-way left turn.
Farm machinery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign means you must stop and yield the right-of-way. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
They rarely use their headlights.
Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and easier to miss. They can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge their speed and distance, so stay alert around motorcyclists.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Always drive at the speed limit.
Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Drive closer to the car in front of you.
Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction on slippery roads. Slow down and do not use cruise control.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Steep hill ahead.
Pedestrians crossing ahead.
Low ground railroad crossing.
Low clearance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the bridge or overpass ahead is low. Do not drive under it if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (13 feet 6 inches in this case).

questions.question: You reach an intersection blocked by traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly until traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front.
Wait outside the intersection until you can drive through completely.
Honk your horn to make cars move forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait outside the intersection until you can drive through completely.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if traffic is stopped on the other side and you cannot drive all the way through. Wait for traffic to clear so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: Your vehicle is in an accident and blocks traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
Do not move your vehicle under any circumstances.
Wait for police to arrive before moving your vehicle.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if possible. Always stay at the scene and give your information to other people involved.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: The posted speed limit.
A speed that is reasonable and safe.
A speed that is safe for current road conditions.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must drive at a reasonable and safe speed. Choose your speed based on the area, traffic, pedestrians, weather, road condition, and lighting. Always follow the legal speed limit.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, what should you do?

options.text: Return to your lane when you have enough space between you and the passed vehicle.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road immediately.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to your lane when you have enough space between you and the passed vehicle.
questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, return to the right side of the road when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
